Planet Bike Big Buck front bike fender The inner fork mounting system is ok, but the fender will move around some horizontally not covering all of tire if you are doing any kind of jumping or trail riding.
I modified the fenders, getting rid of the single expansion screw mount. Removed some metal from the mounts, bent them 90 degrees, and both peices of the front fender now bolt horizontally through the Fork hole (where U brakes used to bolt to on the forks). Testing it on my full rigid fat bike, hucking down some dropoffs and over major roots, the fenders now stay perfectly in place.

I left the rear fender unchanged. However, I put on some grip tape on my seat post where the rear fender mounts to by way of strap/cam. Before the grip tape, the rear fender would move slightly side to side. It is now nearly as stable as the front fenders while still allowing quick removal.

text_fidelity_a:
Flextone Bone Collector Bull Collector Elk Call I bought this elk bugle back in May in anticipation of my elk hunt this Fall. The call is pretty easy to use, and in terms of sound, it did a fine job. The only problem was that yesterday, it was about 30 degrees out in the morning, when I went to expand the tube, and it broke into two pieces. The tube got very brittle in the cold air. I would have thought Flextone would have field tested this design a bit more, but I'm going to contact them and see what they say. I'll post back what I find out.

Update - 12/12/2014:

I promised a follow up, and here it is. I kindly let Flextone know that the tube broke into two pieces, and I mentioned how other Amazon users had the same problem, and I also asked about replacement. I just got a response back from them, and here it is:

"We haven't had an issue with the tube. Unfortunately we don't have any tubing available, but we will have them available at the middle of next year. Please contact us then for pricing and availability."

I was pretty unhappy with this response, so I've lowered my rating from 3 stars to 1 star. It seems they think that if someone other than them has an issue, it's not really an issue. I've dealt with lots of companies that stand behind their products and are willing to accept a design flaw and bend over backwards to help the customer fix/replace it. Not Plano (Flextone). When I bought this product, it only had 2 good reviews, but you can see them getting lower over time now. Do yourself a favor and avoid this bugle. There are better ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Flextone Bone Collector Bull Collector Elk Call

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack T Series Treadmills I ordered this machine to try to do something (beside eating) during quarantine.
My husband put it together in a couple of hours. The only time he needed my help was to assemble the parts that goes under the machine that makes it able to fold.
Once ready it is pretty sturdy. Obviously not as the ones at the gym, but mostly because it is smaller. The “bed” is shorter than the pro, but that’s exactly why it is perfect for a house, in my case for my garage. It is somewhat light weight. You can move it a little.
As soon as you press start it ask you to connect it with IFIT. I did not do that. I pressed the iFit button for 30 seconds and it was override. You CAN use it without the app. BUT, I bought the 5’’ screen. I can’t watch anything more than my stats there. Maybe if you buy the machines with larger screens the iFit app could be a good idea. It depends on your likes. But you can totally use this model without the app (6.5s)
The machine is very smooth. No weird sound beside the normal sound of the belt running.
This machine does not have a fan (I don’t need it) , and has good speakers.
I do mostly sprints, so I move from power walking with encline for 1 minute to all out for 1 minute for 15-20 min, and the machine works perfectly in those speeds and incline changes. It does change the speed fast. So you need to be attentive.
My 5’’ screen shows me cal, distance, time, laps...
The folding process is super easy! And like I said before it is not super heavy, and when going down to the floor is smooth, soft and slow. It does not fall fast.
It has a space where you can put your phone or tablet on the front. 2 cup (or towels or whatever) holders on the sides. And the STOP button with the strap for emergency.
Since “we” put it together I’ve been using it everyday. And I really like it. I could definitely recommended it.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel i have bought some really expensive beds over the past few years and i have done much research to get a good bed. i have not succeeded. so i decided to go with this. TPU does not stretch as many commented on and so it stays inflated. i put a foam 2" topper on top of this and it's like a regular bed, but i think it is better. yes the inflator pump sucks but it does the job. i am not going back to a normal bed. just have to dial in the air pressure now for the ideal feel. i wish i had not spent all that money on the last bed. worth noting that the size can be an issue when fitting sheets. it's in between double and queen size. consider jersey sheets in double since they stretch.

update
ok so the negative vote i got made me think and i realize most of the review is about how regular beds suck and not how this bed is awesome, so time for an update. one of the great features i already mentioned, no stretching or leaks so the bed stays firm. another good feature is the connections inside the bed. the system they use allows for a fairly flat surface because the seal points are not form top to bottom but have a linkage that allows the bed to inflate to a fairly consistent depth across the surface. the image shows it well. other air beds have deep pockets where the weld connects the top to bottom piece. that is a major deal if you have ever slept on an airbed like this. flat surface is key. this bed seems to have the most advanced welding. the only real issue i have is that the bed is so light weight that it moves around easily on the frame. that can be annoying. Costco sells this same item and i sell to Costco so i know how intensely they review items for consideration to sell. this is the best airbed on the market today, period.
text_fidelity_b: Lightspeed Outdoors 2 Person PVC-Free Air Bed Mattress for Camping and Travel

text_fidelity_a: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit When looking for 2 lb weights I opted for these rather than more traditional weights because a) they looked like it would be possible to extend all the fingers while holding the weights if you want more length in the arm.  and b) They seemed to have the weight distributed evenly on both the palm side and the back side of the hand.  Previously, I thought weighted gloves were the answer, but they all have their weight on the back of the hand only, which exercises different muscles than if you were to have the weight mostly in the palm.  After trying out these weights I must say that I'm very happy.  These not only have even weight distribution on both sides of each hand, but you also have the option of letting go your grip and extending your fingers out fully while doing many exercises without worrying about the weights dropping.  The DVD has 3 15 minute workouts which are great for either a warm-up into a more lengthy workout, or for something quick in the morning to wake me up and get me going.  The only issue I have is the videography of the dvd.  The camera person apparently felt there was a need to switch camera angles every 5 seconds.  Very distracting. It wouldn't have bothered me as much if I was able to see the whole body of the instructor more often, but I've done the standing workout is the one I've done the most and often the video shoots the top half of her body without showing what she's doing with her legs... and switches to show her feet and not showing what she's doing with her arms!  I'm sure after I do it several more times I'll be able to just do the upper & lower half movements without needing to see her do them, but when you're first learning a movement is when it's most important to continually see it so that you're sure you get it right.  Especially if you're like me and don't get choreography down very quickly.  It would've been better if they just stuck to one or two camera angles and stayed there rather than switching constantly.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Pilates Total Toning Kit

Western Star Tetherball Game Set - Soft-Touch Tether Ball with Durable Attached Rope - Indoor, Outdoor, Yard, Beach Play - 5 Colors - Easy Attach & Play - A Classic Family Outdoor Game for Kids I'm a grown adult and wanted to get back into the tetherball game. My husband built me a tetherball pole/base as the reviews on standard ones just didn't cut it. However, the base is not a concern in this review.

We've only played with the tetherball a total of 3 times. First time was fine (it was also the very first time my husband had actually played thetherball). But the second time when I played with a friend, the rope from the pole to the ball tore right at the base of the ball. I thought "no big deal I'll just tie it back on"

False. I tied it back on and within 30 minutes, it tore off again. I added on several knots and even went to YouTube to look up sturdy knots but that's not the issue. The string for this ball is VERY flimsy and weak.

On the third go around, the ball came flying off mid-serve and could have injured someone. Ball itself seems to be fine and sturdy. The rope itself, again, is just crappy overall. It keeps breaking and it's not easy to "re-string", if you will.

Overall, the ball is great and seems to be sturdy. However, if you're a grown adult looking into smacking the heck out of a tetherball, definitely be prepared to get a new, sturdier rope because the one that comes with it just doesn't cut it.
text_fidelity_b: Western Star Tetherball Game Set - Soft-Touch Tether Ball with Durable Attached Rope - Indoor, Outdoor, Yard, Beach Play - 5 Colors - Easy Attach & Play - A Classic Family Outdoor Game for Kids

3V Recon Tanto First off I have to say that I bought this Cold Steel Recon Tanto from another source at half of the price offered on Amazon. But after removing it from the packaging and handling it for a while, I can tell you that even at the Amazon price, this is a great value. Yes, you can buy a better version of this knife from Jake Hoback, but you will be spending almost three times the money for incremental improvements. In my case, I would have had to pay five times the money. Like most collectors I have several "safe queens" but at this price I don't feel bad about using and abusing this well-made tool.

Your first glance at this knife will confirm its utilitarian/industrial good looks. It is obviously a knife that is built strongly to be used in tough tasks. Don't bother confirming the blade sharpness with the paper cutting test, you can simply look at the edge under a good light and see the small serrations that line the cutting edge. If you want to be bold and test it with your finger, TREAD LIGHTLY! Cold Steel has taken a thick piece of steel and tapered it into a razor-sharp blade. You will even be able to feel the small serrations pulling at your skin as you touch the edge.

Good useful length, full tang, great balance, sticky rubber grip, this tool inspires great confidence when you hold it. Take a look at some of the posted videos to see what types of abuse this knife has been subjected to and survived handily. If I had to leave our home suddenly and enter the woods and swamp lands of Southwest Florida, I'd probably select my Busse Hellrazor to take with me. On the other hand, if I showed up at a rendezvous point with a Cold Steel Recon Tanto, no one would laugh at me. They know better.

PS: A decent (not great) kydex sheath is included. If you're like me, you don't like a sheath hanging off your belt that can catch on various objects and/or make noise while you're trying to be quiet. A simple band threaded through the lower part of the sheath will keep it secure against your thigh.
text_fidelity_b: 3V Recon Tanto

SKLZ Gold Flex Golf Swing Trainer Warm-Up Stick I bought this for my son, with the goal of helping his timing and strength. So far, I have been very please with the purchase. The trainer is made with high quality materials, and feels very solid. It is easy for him to sing in the yard, and I have noticed it is helping his tempo. It also gives him something slightly weighted to swing while he works on his shoulder turn.

The 3 main uses for this trainer are
1. Practice tempo. Swinging the trainer for 20 minutes or so a few times a week or at the range will help you feel the speed of your swing.

2. Warming up. Before a round or practice, this is a great tool to get loose.

3. Strength training. I put this last because if this is your only goal, you may want a slightly heavier club to swing. Swinging this daily will help build good muscle memory and strength in the right muscles.

He is 11, and the 40" size is perfect for him, and will last him for a few years. I am a little over 6', and while I can use it, I will likely get myself the 48" version soon.

text_fidelity_a:
Niceday Elliptical Machine, Elliptical Trainer for Home with Hyper-Quiet Magnetic Driving System, 16 Resistance Levels, 15.5IN Stride, 400LBS Weight Capacity Expect a BIG box to arrive! This sucker weighs about 100lbs. So you may need help to move it & get it unboxed.

The manufacturer states 90% assembled, but it's probably more like 50%. The flywheel & deck components will come pre-assembled. You are in charge of basically 5 main assembly groups: the feet/legs, the vertical tube screws, the handles, the console (computer) & finally the pedals. All tools are included to allow you to get right to work.

It's not a hard assembly, but the documentation isn't the easiest to follow. Luckily, the manufacturer has an assembly video on their Amazon listing. So if you need help, definitely check that out. In fact, you may want to watch it first.

The most cumbersome part of the assembly is the feet/legs. This is b/c you must hold up the entire unit (front or back) to get the respective leg on. If you have a helper, then this will be easy. If, however, you're a lone wolf, then use something to "jack" up the bike. It makes this part MUCH easier. I had a scrap piece of 2x4 that I used (see pic) & it was very helpful.

Once the feet are on, you will move on to the vertical tube screws, then handles, then console & lastly, the computer. Again, these are all very easy parts to put together. Just lay out all parts first, watch the video & review which bolt/screw goes where BEFORE you start the assembly. It will make a big difference towards minimizing your frustration.

Also, BE AWARE that some bolts ARE ALREADY PRE-SCREWED INTO THE BIKE. So they will not be in the bolt bag. For example, I found this was the case for the pulse handle.

Once assembled, the bike works exactly as advertised. It's near silent, very compact (for an elliptical), but still feels very roomy, has 16 levels of resistance (magnetic) controlled by an adjustment dial & has a number of functions & biometrics that can be tracked such as distance, calories burned, time, etc..

Please note - to track PULSE, you must hold the center handles (called the PULSE HANDLES) as there are sensors built in that your palms will contact. However, if you remove your grip, then the pulse biometric will disappear from the computer screen.

A more accurate method, would be to use a fitness tracker (like a FitBit, Apple Watch or dozens of other makes & models). This way you can track all of your stats in one place (steps, cals burned, distance, etc..) & have that data logged in your smartwatch app. Plus your stats will be far more accurate than the built-in computer on the bike.

However, for convenience & simplicity, the bike computer will do just fine. One option that I would have liked to have seen is a built in light in the LCD panel. If you're in a room with low light then the display can be hard to read.

It's worth mentioning that there's no external power required to run this bike. So you don't need to plug into an outlet. The computer will need 2x AA batteries. However, the manufacturer conveniently ships these with the bike.

So, to wrap things up, the build is going to take a little time, but nothing you can't handle! Once assembled, this bike is very comfortable to use & definitely feels well constructed for a consumer level elliptical. I think the price of $550 w/ free shipping (using Prime & a $50 coupon - at the time of this review) is very fair for this unit.

Overall, this is a great elliptical that will help you meet your daily step, cardio or high intensity workout goals. I definitely can recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Niceday Elliptical Machine, Elliptical Trainer for Home with Hyper-Quiet Magnetic Driving System, 16 Resistance Levels, 15.5IN Stride, 400LBS Weight Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
MSC® Boat Center Console Cover, Color Gray,Pacific Blue Available It seems OK ...

I'm giving it five stars to start with because it is what it said it would be and it fits my center console very well. It looks a lot nicer than the green plastic tarp I was using to keep my console dry. I ordered and received the gray color option.

It's fairly lightweight and folds/rolls up into a nice small package when it's stored in the bag that came with the cover. Most boaters will appreciate that as stowage on a boat is always at a premium. Putting it in its little bag keeps it from catching the wind and blowing away when towing the boat or on the water.

I've only had it for a couple of weeks so time will tell regarding longevity. The problem with most of these things is that they either last or they don't. If it falls apart in an unreasonable amount of time I'll be back to add to this review. I consider 5 years on a fabric cover of any type to be a "reasonable amount of time" for them to remain serviceable. Properly treated exterior grade fabrics should last quite a while. I have a Bimini top that has been on my boat for 15 years and it's still in serviceable condition. The top is deployed from April to October and I tow the boat with it up (it's only 3 miles to the ramp and it's 45 MPH or less speed limit all the way) so that's a good example of good service from an exterior grade fabric.

For some reason unknown to me the drawstring is NOT as shown in the item description. It's not on the aft side of the console where the drawstring and the cutout are located in the picture. It's on the starboard side of the console. Which is a little irritating because that's the side I usually store tackle boxes, coolers etc. to keep them handy to the helm and the fore deck both. So I have to move stuff around to use this console cover, which is not a big deal or a deal killer but I do wish these sellers would get their act together and provide ACCURATE pictures of what they're selling and we're buying.

Because while I like online shopping for the huge array of choices and the availability of things I may or may not find locally, or may have to drive miles to find and still might not be successful -- online shopping is always a crapshoot. You can't pick up and look at what you're buying, you can't walk in a store and see it set up on display so that you can examine its construction and quality. All you have to go by are pictures, item description and subjective reviews of others who have purchased the item. So it would seem to me that if sellers don't want to get returns and charge-backs they ought to pay very close attention to their pictures and item descriptions.
text_fidelity_b: MSC® Boat Center Console Cover, Color Gray,Pacific Blue Available

text_fidelity_a: Chariot SideCarrier 1 Child Side Mounted Child Carrier I have owned this carrier for 3 years and I have to say that chariot makes the highest quality carriers on the market in my opinion. The negatives that I found are. 1, the tire wear. 2, the hitch weighs 1Lb 10oz and if you have a bike with expensive light weight components and your concerned about your bikes total weight this is problem, and it's not practical to remove the hitch when not in use. 3, if you ride on sidewalks the total width of the bike & carrier may be problem depending on you cycling skills. 4, if you use panniers on the right side of the bike it will affect your right turning ability. 5, clearance issues if you have a front fender. The unit handles very well. Other than that it's a very cool design and you surely wont run into many people using the sidecar.

I would find another helmet. I wasted money returning two of these helmets. I bought a Giro that fits great and is more customizable for cheaper. I sent K2 an email and never got a response. I'm done with that company. Don't buy this helmet.

We both feel like the towel itself is very thin, and being this thin would likely not do great for drying one off. It would be something we would keep as a backup or the towel we’d throw on the chair, but not use for actually drying. The Ten Toes paddle is considerably lighter than the Tower one, but still feels pretty sturdy. It floats. You can see some "pool noodle" type foam through the small holes in the adjusting piece. Easy to adjust, and I like this adjustment mechanism better than the Tower one. I took one star off because the top T handle feels kind of cheap, but it is comfortable to use. It took a while to get used to not being securely attached to the bike (feet were bouncing off on rough terrain) but once I got the hang of being on a platform things improved quickly. Along the way I have whacked some rocks very hard on multiple occasions but the Saints have just shrugged that off and kept right on going. I would also recommend, as others have, that you remove the washers from between the studs and the pedal and add the additional studs. If you're looking for some affordable, rugged platforms look no further.

text_fidelity_a:
Lite Holster Stretch, Expandable, Secure Flashlight Holder with Belt Clip, Universal Sizing, Black My use is for 1" diameter by 5" long tactical lights which do not protrude out the bottom. I also tried it with a 2 C cell light which protrudes out the bottom a lot.

I was looking for something either with a flap cover or a snug but easy to insert fit. This is neither. It has no cover flap, but has a VERY snug fit on this type of light. However it is made up of a series of internal flaps and elastic straps you have to guide the light through to get it into this case. You cannot easily do this one handed as you have to spread two internal flaps apart and hold them that way to insert the light. In addition if you have to sit/stand as in driving patrol or the like, the light works it's way out the top even if it doesn't protrude out the bottom. Since there is nothing to lock it in, the movement of sitting and moving around when seated pushes against the bottom squeezing the light upward like squeezing a toothpaste tube. Eventually it pops out the top. In addition if your light has a tailcap switch it will get turned on without your knowing it in daytime (you would see the light at night), draining the batteries, as there is nothing protecting the tailcap switch from being pressed against the seat bottom.

From my experience with it, this is pretty useless if you are going to be wearing it on a belt in the vertical position, whether a short small diameter or longer larger diameter light. As a temporary worklight holder it isn't bad, but how often do you need a worklight on your belt?
text_fidelity_b: Lite Holster Stretch, Expandable, Secure Flashlight Holder with Belt Clip, Universal Sizing, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Advanced Elements FireFly Inflatable Kayak I purchased this kayak primarily for bays and lakes, but now that I've braved the ocean with it, I'm convinced this is a great, sturdy kayak! It is quite wide, so while initially it seems like it doesn't keep a straight line as well as the slimmer, hard-shell kayaks, I think this is a positive point for intermediate/casual users like myself. Out on the ocean, the kayak didn't rock too much, and withstood 2-3 foot swells with ease.

The only thing I don't really like is that it doesn't have any "machinery" for the clip-on seats with some back support. I've learned that wearing a small backpack helps with back support, but as is, the kayak is not "tall" enough for you to comfortably sit and lean into.

It is very easy to inflate and then put away, and I found all the instructions very self-evident. Overall, I think this is a great option for anyone looking to save a bit of room in their storage options, and appreciates a bit of a wider load for stability and speed.
text_fidelity_b: Advanced Elements FireFly Inflatable Kayak

text_fidelity_a: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu I quite like this bottle.  I bought this in the 16 oz size and i maybe should have gone larger, as i really like the design.  I use this one for coffee, though If it were larger i would keep water in it.  The thing I like about this over others in the Kleen Kanteen range is the lip and threading.  The classic bottles have threading on the outside of the lip of the bottle with a cap which screws over the lip, clamping its edge against a gasket.  I have come to find this design prone to leaks if the gasket isn't properly seated.  The TKWide range just doesn't have this problem.  The threading is on the inside, low, under the lip of the bottle and the cap screws into it with a simple o ring.  I'm not a huge fan of the "cafe cap" but i just remove it and drink from the lip of the bottle which is itself quite comfortable.  It's kleer that kleen kanteen designed this bottle to work in exactly this way, as the lip of the bottle is the most comfortable of any i've ever encountered to drink from and they even make an assortment of different caps for this line with different features.  I'm considering getting the simple steel loop or bamboo cap to eliminate all remaining unnecessary parts.  The user experience drinking from the bottle with cap removed is similar to drinking from a tall glass tumbler.  The threading is recessed from the lip and doesn't interfere with drinking at all.. I also like that the 'cafe cap' is easily disassembled.. I hate cleaning these things, once a few weeks of coffee residue gets on them.  I've dropped this bottle twice and it has a dent now, but nothing severe.  I find it well made and well engineered and though, in my head at least, this bottle rivals the yeti ramblers which are similar, its about half of the price or less.
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen TKWide 16oz (w/Café Cap) - Tofu

text_fidelity_a: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills There is one huge flaw in this machine...and that is if you intend to use the incline feature you will no longer be able to reach anything out in front of you, meaning you can not reach your water bottle...music device...digital read out display...or even to use the heart rate grip handles.  If you look at the machine in the pictures...you will notice a black plastic insert that runs on top of the actual tread mill just below the display.  As you incline the machine...this part of the treadmill comes closer to you....meaning you have to move more backwards on the machine in order to avoid stepping on it.  You have to move back so far that you literally have to bend over at the waist just to use the heart rate grips.  I found myself keep having to step on the sides off the treadmill and stop my walk anytime I wanted to change my music or change a feature on the unit.  Very very frustrating. If you walk for say 30 to 60 minutes and you watch videos on youtube or something like that...you will have to literally stop walking and step off the machine as many times as the videos run out...or your music choice changes.  I don't hold onto the rail in front of me anyway, but if you are someone who does...you will not be able to do so with the unit inclined.  You will keep stepping on the plastic piece and can literally injure yourself the first time you do it.  Machine seems nice otherwise but this is to huge of a flaw to give it anything but 1 star.  I guess everyone else is not using the incline feature.  And no...I am not 8 feet tall....with long legs. Only 5'10" and my wife is 5'1" and has the same issue.  Just note the above and take into consideration when purchasing. I wouldn't buy this unit again...and already put together and box tore up to return.  Frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

Mine has a manufacturing flaw where the handle on the valve to the lower tank does not completely clear the plastic of the unit when closing. It sits right up against the edge of the plastic, and if you move the thing around too much, or if it changes temperature substantially (e.g. in the trunk of a vehicle) then the handle gets pushed out a tiny bit. That opens the lower tank *just enough* that gasses seep out. I had it in my shed for a few days and came back and the whole shed reeked of that tank.

I will still use the thing but not in an enclosed building or similar. In a standup tent it should be fine. Maybe mine is just an outlier in material thickness or something.

text_fidelity_a:
Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ This is the best thermos I've owned to date, but it's far from perfect.

If you put piping hot coffee in it, it will keep it hot for about 45 minutes, and keep it warm for about 2 more hours after that. I haven't used it for cold drinks.

I love the handle style; that's my favorite part about it. Most handled thermoses have this infuriating issue of the mouthpiece never lining up properly with where the handle is, so you always have to hold them weirdly to drink from them. On this thermos, the handle is fabric, and can be adjusted 360 degrees around the thermos, so no matter where the mouthpiece ends up, you can just adjust the handle to be right where you need it. the other nice thing about the fabric handle is that you won't break it by bumping it into things or dropping it.

The worst part about this thing is cleaning it. The entire head of it is very complex, with lots of moving parts, springs, and plastic bits - ALL of which are submerged in whatever you are drinking. So, when you take the lid off, you have disassemble the whole thing and either soak all the parts, or wash them all individually. Don't be lazy and put off cleaning it until the next day or you'll have whatever you drank caked all though the innards. If you don't mind keeping it clean, it's really nice. I'm very happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley The Quadvac Trigger Action Mug, Canvas, 16OZ

HOPSOOKEN 30L Ultra Lightweight Travel Water Resistant Packable Backpack for Hiking Cycling Sports Daypack Backpack/Ultralight and Handy (Black New) This is a lightweight (in all aspects) bag that is great for limited purposes. It is made out of extremely thin and flexible material. It can fold up into itself and zip up (see picture) for easy storage and transport when not using it to carry items in. I can see this bag as being an excellent option for travelers who might find themselves needing another bag/storage option at the last minute. Like when you realize at the airport your bag is overweight and to avoid a huge baggage fee, you wish you had a small bag you could put some heavy items in and carry it on the plane instead. This would be perfect for that. Or you spend the holidays with relatives and they send you home with more goodies for the kids than you have room in your luggage for.

It's not a primary use bag. There is no padding at all. Not in the bottom of the bag. Not in the shoulder straps. There is no protection for items within the bag or your shoulders. It would not be comfortable carrying this with anything substantial or heavy inside. The material reminds me of an inexpensive windbreaker or poncho.

Pros:
Great backup bag for unexpected situations
Lightweight and very compact
Folds and zips into itself for easy storage and transport

Cons:
Flimsy shoulder straps with no padding
Questionable ability to carry heavy, rigid items like books or glass bottles
No padding in the bag itself, thus no protection for items inside

I received this bag for minimal cost in exchange for my unbiased review.
